tapeLine: Wednesday 18 November: S&P 500 −16.90 (−0.23%) to 7,323.63, a fifth straight loss and the longest losing streak since June; Dow −561.25 (−1.11%) to 50,198.17; Nasdaq Composite +101.50 (+0.42%) to 24,429.89 (StockTitan; Vista PGlobal; Cappnotes, 18 Nov). Business Upturn carries slightly different closes; the majority figures are used.
matters:
Nvidia’s overnight futures lift did not hold Wednesday: the stock fell about 2.9% despite its beat-and-raise, the Dow dropped more than 1% as managed-care stocks sold off on regulatory concerns, and the S&P 500 slipped below its 200-day moving average while the Nasdaq edged up (Cappnotes; Benzinga; Motley Fool, 18 Nov). October housing starts jumped 9.9% to a 1.309M annual rate against a ~1.23M consensus, while permits fell 7.4% to 1.295M (Census via NAHB, Seeking Alpha, 18 Nov).

Minutes of the 27–28 October FOMC meeting showed almost all participants judging further rate increases likely appropriate, with a couple saying more than 25 bp could warrant consideration in December; the hold at 3.75%–4.00% drew two dissents (Cook, Hammack) in favour of a hike (Federal Reserve; OptionsPilot; Seeking Alpha, 18 Nov). After the close Anthropic priced its upsized IPO at $83, above the $70–$78 range, raising about $81 billion; ANT begins trading on Nasdaq today (CNBC; TechCrunch; Washington Post, 18 Nov). Nasdaq-100 futures were up about 2% early Thursday, with Walmart reporting before the open (Invezz; Reuters via Investing.com, 19 Nov).

alsoOnTape: 10-year Treasury yield fell about 3 bp to roughly 5.07% Wednesday (Cappnotes, citing Treasury data; Investrade 5.065%, 18 Nov). The dollar index rose about 0.3% to around 103.80, described as a 19-month high (Cappnotes; Benzinga, 18 Nov). Oil, gold and VIX closes were not found with a clean dated source and are left out.
overnight: Latest confirmed close — Wednesday 18 November: S&P 500 7,323.63 (−0.23%); Nasdaq Composite 24,429.89 (+0.42%); Dow 50,198.17 (−561.25, −1.11%) (StockTitan; Vista PGlobal, 18 Nov).
Nvidia — reversed premarket gains to close down about 2.9% (Cappnotes); Vista PGlobal gives $150.96, −$4.50; Finwire −2.4% (18 Nov). The range is noted rather than a single figure.

Anthropic IPO — priced at $83 a share, above the $70–$78 range; about 980 million shares, roughly $81.3 billion raised, described as the largest IPO on record (CNBC; StockTitan; Axios, 18 Nov). Valuation figures differ by basis (about $1.08–1.1 trillion non-diluted, about $1.5 trillion fully diluted) and are reported, not confirmed by a filing here.

Futures — early Thursday 19 Nov: Nasdaq-100 futures up about 2.1%, S&P 500 futures up about 1.1%, Dow futures up about 0.7%; other snapshots show smaller gains (Invezz; Reuters via Investing.com, 19 Nov).
macro: Housing starts, October — 1.309M annualized, +9.9% from 1.191M in September and above a ~1.23M consensus; single-family +4.0% to 864K; multifamily +23.6% to 445K; permits −7.4% to 1.295M. Census notes the monthly change is within its ±16.8% confidence interval (NAHB Eye on Housing; Seeking Alpha; FXTribune, 18 Nov).

FOMC minutes (27–28 Oct) — hold at 3.75%–4.00% on a 10–2 vote, Cook and Hammack dissenting for a 25 bp hike. Summaries say almost all participants saw further increases as likely appropriate and a couple floated more than 25 bp for December; staff flagged risks around AI-related debt. Summaries differ in emphasis; exact wording is in the Fed release (Federal Reserve; OptionsPilot; Seeking Alpha, 18 Nov). Next meeting 8–9 Dec.
flow: Breadth, dealer gamma, put-call and skew are paid data and are not on this page.

regime.tag: Five straight S&P 500 losses and a break of the 200-day average, with minutes pointing to more hikes and the 10-year near 5.07%, into the Anthropic debut.
regime.sizing: Whether a ~2% Nasdaq futures gap on the Anthropic debut survives the open, Walmart and Hammack is unresolved.

secondOrder: Wednesday split by index: the Nasdaq rose while the Dow fell over 1%, so the selling came from managed care and blue chips rather than tech, a change from the AI-led declines earlier in the week. Hawkish minutes and the 10-year still eased about 3 bp, extending the pattern of stocks and yields moving down together. Observations, not forecasts.

scorecard.text: The prior brief reported index futures higher early Wednesday after Nvidia (S&P futures +0.4% to +0.8%, Dow +0.1% to +0.3%). Only the Nasdaq held up (+0.42%); the S&P 500 closed −0.23% and the Dow −1.11% (StockTitan, 18 Nov). Nvidia itself fell about 2.9% (Cappnotes, 18 Nov).
The prior brief carried a housing-starts consensus of 1.27M (Finviz) and 1.230M (Investing.com). The print was 1.309M, above both (NAHB, 18 Nov).

The prior brief reported Anthropic expected to price Wednesday evening at the top of the $70–$78 range or above, with trading Thursday. It priced at $83, above the range, and lists today (CNBC; TechCrunch, 18 Nov).
The prior brief listed the FOMC minutes at 2:00 ET for a 10–2 hold at 3.75%–4.00%. They were released as scheduled and confirm that vote (Federal Reserve, 18 Nov).
The prior brief said whether Nvidia’s futures lift would hold through the minutes and Anthropic pricing was unresolved. It did not hold for the S&P 500 or Dow; no direction had been called.
